correctness.rationale: The proof reduces insertion distance exactly to \(qk-C_k(w)\), where \(C_k(w)\) is a maximum contiguous-partition coverage statistic. A refinement argument proves \(C_k(w)\ge\min\{n,q+k-1\}\) for every full-support word, and the heavy-symbol family attains equality. Boundary cases \(q\ge2\), \(n\ge q\), and \(k\ge1\) are included. Independent finite replay agrees with the literal supersequence definition on tiny cases and exhaustively checks broader finite ranges; no finite experiment is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Worst-case distance to a target language is a natural extremal companion to the known per-instance edit-distance problem. The theorem gives a complete all-parameter insertion radius, a sharp transition between the length-deficiency term \(qk-n\) and the symbol-distribution term \((q-1)(k-1)\), and an explicit extremizer. It is neither a routine finite census nor a mere renaming of the known dynamic program.
